hash_validation_boundary: The product map legend and prior roof coordinate-mapping audit have recorded SHA-256 values but no independent expected self-checksum in the committed input set; their bytes are recorded, and their graph, legend, reconciliation, linker, and source-audit references are cross-checked against the corresponding files.

All artifacts with an upstream expected checksum are verified against that checksum before graph matching; both pre-reconciliation source PDBs and corrected candidate PDBs are checked against reconciliation/linker records.

ambiguity_and_mapping_assumptions: The six map IDs 78-83 used in the roof-only precursor search are fixed to candidate tail/azide anchors from the prior linker mapping audit; this does not authorize those anchors as source chemistry evidence.
Complete-product exact mappings are enumerated without fixing the prior candidate labels. The graph matcher compares element labels and simple adjacency only.
PDB CONECT resolves by atom serial. PDB LINK resolves only by a unique full chain, residue, insertion code, altloc, and atom-name identity.

Source bond-label-preserving automorphisms define mapping equivalence classes. Distinct classes remain separate because they can transfer different source bond labels onto the unlabeled PDB adjacency.
PDB coordinates do not choose among exact mappings or bond-label transfer classes; geometry is reported after mapping as a screen only.
PDB atom names, including the open/closed aliases for map 79 and map 90, are candidate coordinate labels and are not source-authoritative atom names.

source_product_graph.source_assignment_basis: Nature Fig. 2a directly draws the product with the roof propyl substituent bonded to triazole N1 and the B29 linker substituent bonded to C4. This assigns source azide N attached to C23 as N1, internal alkyne carbon C7 as C4, and terminal alkyne carbon C8 as C5. The atom assignment follows the primary product drawing, not PDB adjacency or distances.

bond_order_representation.smiles_bond_form: Explicit Kekulé single/double bonds are written for the new linker and click ring; RDKit sanitization perceives the triazole ring as aromatic.
bond_order_representation.consumed_terminal_alkyne: The precursor C7≡C8 triple bond is consumed; C7 map 88 and C8 map 89 are triazole ring atoms in the product.

representation_boundaries.roof_carboxyl_groups: All three macrocycle carboxyl groups retain the neutral COOH form drawn in the source: map groups [52,53,54], [60,61,62], and [68,69,70]. This is a graph representation choice, not a physiological protonation assignment.
representation_boundaries.lys_b29_cut: Map 92 is the NZ endpoint, represented as NH2 to cap the isolated graph and satisfy valence. The LysB29 CE continuation and all other insulin atoms are outside this graph. The computed total-hydrogen formula therefore describes this capped graph and is not the hydrogen formula of the actual conjugate.
representation_boundaries.stereochemistry: No stereochemistry is introduced beyond the source graph; the product drawing does not define additional stereocentres at the B29 linker or triazole.

source_roof_graph_precursor.interpretation: The two source roof automorphisms are a precursor symmetry result; the complete clicked product is audited separately.

geometry_screen_method.purpose: Conservative broad plausibility screen for mapped heavy-heavy coordinate distances.

basis.citation: B. Cordero et al., Covalent radii revisited, Dalton Trans. 2008, 2832-2838, DOI: 10.1039/B801115J.

geometry_screen_method.interval_definition: For each source bond class, add the tabulated low and high heuristic offsets to the sum of the two element covalent radii.
interpretation_limits: These numeric intervals are a conservative geometry screen, not bond-order evidence.
Distances are not used to select, rank, or reject graph mappings.
All mapped edges are retained, including those outside the screen.
The PDB adjacency records do not encode bond order, charge, or stereochemistry.

assessment.interpretation: The complete 92-node, 99-edge source product graph has an exact element-labeled adjacency isomorphism to each selected corrected PDB target. Each state has 16 exact map-to-coordinate assignments; map IDs 78-92 are consistent and unique across them, while roof/scaffold map IDs retain ambiguity. The two bond-label-preserving source roof automorphisms are reported as a precursor result. Source bond labels are transferred only after mapping and the PDB records remain adjacency-only. Coordinates are screened against disclosed broad heuristic intervals and do not validate bond order or mapping. The source drawing supports the 1,4-disubstituted product graph; the PDB adjacency alone does not independently establish bond order or distinguish bond-label/regioisomer assignments where multiple symmetry classes remain.
assessment.mismatch_handling: If any exact isomorphism is absent, or unmatched target atoms/edges remain, the corresponding state reports the unmatched inventory and cannot support a unique topology assignment. If multiple source bond-label mapping classes remain, the audit reports unresolved bond-label/regioisomer assignment ambiguity and does not claim a unique topology.
limitations: Corrected candidate PDBs are model-coordinate derivatives, not experimentally resolved NNC2215 structures.
PDB CONECT and LINK records are adjacency-only; bond orders, formal charges, stereochemistry, and protonation are not validated here.
The source product graph represents the source-supported click product connectivity and does not establish simulation-pH protonation or force-field parameters.
The geometry intervals are intentionally broad heuristic screens and do not establish chemical bonds or regioisomer identity.
Hydrogen neighbor labels and counts reproduce model CONECT records and are not validated chemistry.
